summary: Complete the frozen event-platform delivery correctness chain with a tenant-scoped immutable PostgreSQL consumer inbox, stable logical-consumer identity, canonical-event fingerprint collision detection, transaction-scoped duplicate serialization, and same-transaction PostgreSQL business effects without claiming distributed exactly-once behavior.

impacts.evidence: Every receipt is keyed by organization/workspace/consumer/event and protected by forced SELECT/INSERT RLS; processor input must match the EventBus envelope tenant before any handler work begins.
Inbox storage deliberately excludes the business event payload and persists only the SHA-256 canonical-envelope fingerprint plus bounded delivery metadata, minimizing duplicate PII retention.
No REST/OpenAPI surface changes; this is an internal consumer transaction/idempotency boundary.
Deduplication is based on the exact canonical Task-007 EventBus envelope fingerprint; retry attempt/backoff metadata is intentionally excluded so the immutable event identity remains stable.
No connector/plugin SDK surface or provider-specific branch is introduced.

High-risk expand migration 000008 creates inbox_receipts while preserving the pre-Task-009 inbox_events placeholder deny-all, allowing old readers/writers and new binaries to coexist during rolling qualification.

Transaction-scoped advisory locking serializes the same tenant/consumer/event identity, fingerprint mismatch fails closed, receipts are immutable, hard mutation is blocked, and no arbitrary handler error or event payload is persisted.
Inbox deduplicates already-authorized event handling and neither grants approvals nor bypasses Task 017 risk/approval decisions.

Stable consumer identity, event ID/type, fingerprint, first-observed time and committed attempt provide deterministic evidence that one logical consumer applied one immutable event without duplicating its business payload.

Duplicate redelivery returns success without calling business code; crash before PostgreSQL commit leaves neither side effects nor receipt, while crash after commit causes the next delivery to observe the immutable receipt and skip side effects. Event-ID reuse with different content is a permanent collision.
Direct remote side effects are explicitly outside the inbox atomicity guarantee and must use an outbox or provider idempotency key; no webhook delivery behavior is changed here.
Receipt processed time/attempt and EventBus duplicate/collision counters can support duplicate-rate and poison-event telemetry without storing raw payloads or errors.

Migration 000008 is additive; rollback disables the new inbox-aware consumer binary while retaining immutable receipts and the old deny-all placeholder. Backup/restore rehearsal preserves receipt rows and RLS.

Tests cover consumer/fingerprint validation, handler-once behavior, duplicate fast-path, collision rejection, crash/retry with no premature receipt, tenant mismatch, advisory-lock namespacing, immutable/RLS migration shape, contracts, and restore rehearsal.
